_strings.@@df5c90e914f8: Colorado Earned Income Tax Credit (COEITC) - SSN filers — Full-year or part-year Colorado residents who claim the federal Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC). Part-year residents apportion by the DR 0104PN line 34 percentage (capped at 100%). (ITIN filers, filers whose SSN is not valid for employment, and certain filers under 25 without qualifying children use form DR 0104TN and claim on DR 0104CR line 9 instead — and a federal-EITC claimant who had to leave out dependents only because of an ITIN/invalid SSN may claim a HIGHER COEITC on line 9.)
_strings.@@e987416ffd3a: TABOR State Sales Tax Refund (claimed on the 2025 return) — Full-year Colorado residents born before 2007 (or full-year residents under eighteen who are required to file a return). The return must be postmarked or transmitted by the extension due date (October 15, 2026). In general you must be 18 or older as of January 1, 2025; if under 18 as of that date you must either have a Colorado tax liability (DR 0104 line 13 greater than 0) or be claiming a refund of Colorado wage withholding on a W-2. You must not have been convicted of a felony and incarcerated in a Colorado Department of Corrections or Federal Bureau of Prisons facility for 180 days or more during the year. A deceased person must have met all requirements as of the date of death. Lines 34-37 of the 2025 DR 0104 compute a Modified AGI solely to size the refund; they do not affect the income tax computation.

_strings.@@f0d1fb8990b9: Treaty conformity — CO conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from CO income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the CO return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Colorado's DR 0104 begins at "Federal Taxable Income" (2025 line 1, "from your federal income tax form 1040, 1040 SR, or 1040 SP line 15"). Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal taxable income, so it flows through to Colorado untaxed UNLESS Colorado has an explicit addback. The 2025 DR 0104's complete Additions to Federal Taxable Income are Lines 2-7 plus Line 9 (Line 8 is "Reserved for future use"): state income tax addback (Schedule A), Qualified Business Income Deduction addback, Standard/Itemized Federal Deduction addback (federal AGI over $300,000), business meals deducted under IRC 274(k), nonqualified CollegeInvest Tuition Savings Account distributions, nonqualified Colorado ABLE Account distributions, and Line 9 "Other Additions" — whose enumerated items in the 2025 booklet are: non-Colorado state/local bond interest (net of amortized premiums/expenses; Colorado bonds issued on or after May 1, 1980 are excluded from the addback), a federal charitable deduction for a conservation easement also claimed for a Colorado credit, expenses for unauthorized alien labor services, fiduciary adjustments and Colorado K-1 (DR 0106K) additions from a partnership or S corporation, expenses at/payments to a club that restricts membership on the basis of sex, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, marital status, race, creed, religion, color, ancestry or national origin, and forfeited employer contributions to a home savings account previously subtracted. NONE of these is an addback of federally treaty-exempt or foreign-source income. Therefore treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed and Colorado conforms. (Confirmed against the official 2025 Book 104 and the standalone 2025 DR 0104 form PDF on tax.colorado.gov.)

state_tax.work_common_tail: 0. Tax line: DR 0104 Line 13 (Colorado Tax): full-year residents take the amount from the 2025 booklet tax table (built at 4.4%) for Line 12 Colorado Taxable Income (= Line 10 subtotal minus Line 11 DR 0104AD subtractions); for taxable income over $50,000 the booklet worksheet multiplies Line 12 by 4.4% (.044); part-year residents and nonresidents transfer the apportioned tax from DR 0104PN line 36. This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Rate change: the 2025 rate is 4.4% (.044) — BACK UP from the temporarily reduced 4.25% of tax year 2024, and equal to the 2023 rate. The 2025 DR 0104 Book prints 4.4% three independent ways (the Line 13 instructions "The income tax rate is currently 4.4%", the "2025 Colorado Income Tax Table with tax rate of 4.4%" header, and the over-$50,000 worksheet's "Multiply by 4.4% X .044"), and the printed booklet is the sole authority for the year's rate — never substitute a TABOR-adjusted figure from another year. Colorado starts from federal TAXABLE income (DR 0104 Line 1, Form 1040 line 15) — the federal standard/itemized deduction is already embedded, so Colorado has no exemptions and no separate standard deduction. (Colorado does ADD BACK part of a large federal deduction: DR 0104 Line 4, for filers with federal AGI over $300,000.) 2025 line renumbering: additions are Lines 2-7, Line 8 is "Reserved for future use", Other Additions moved to Line 9, subtotal Line 10 (sum of lines 1-7 and line 9), DR 0104AD subtractions Line 11, Colorado Taxable Income Line 12, Colorado Tax Line 13 (2024: subtotal 9, subtractions 10, taxable income 11, tax 12; 2023: taxable income 10, tax 11). Never carry a line number between years. The DR 0104 form itself does not print a multiplication — Line 13 says to use the tax table (or the DR 0104PN apportionment). For 2025 the printed table stops at $50,000 and the worksheet covers taxable incomes over $50,000 (the same cutoff as the 2024 DR 0104 Book, printed page 38). The table is built at 4.4% but its $100-band midpoint rounding can differ from raw multiplication by a dollar or two; the printed table row controls on the filed form. Not modeled by calc.state_tax: Line 14 Alternative Minimum Tax, Line 15 recapture of prior-year credits, the Line 17 nonrefundable credits (DR 0104CR line 65) and Line 31 refundable credits (DR 0104CR line 26), and the TABOR State Sales Tax Refund on Lines 34-38 (Modified AGI is computed there solely to size the refund and does not affect the tax).
